case.short_input: Weak frontend resume vs Frontend Intern JD
case.expected: Low-to-mid score; flags missing TypeScript, testing, REST; rewrites vague bullets without inventing metrics

analysis.score_reason: Partial alignment: core JavaScript, React and Git skills present; relevant React project shown with usage stats; measurable impact limited to one project; several required skills (TypeScript, REST API, responsive CSS, unit testing) missing; keywords and domain language partially covered; resume is readable but could be more concise and impact‑focused.

missing_skills.jd_evidence: Experience with TypeScript in a real project
Familiarity with REST API integration and handling asynchronous state
Working knowledge of responsive CSS and cross-browser testing
Exposure to unit testing with Jest or a similar framework

weak_bullet_ids.original: Did a project on web development using HTML, CSS and some JavaScript.
weak_bullet_ids.problem: Vague description; lacks specifics about role, technologies depth, or impact

weak_bullet_ids.original: Worked on the company website and fixed bugs.
weak_bullet_ids.problem: Generic statement without details on contributions or outcomes
Unspecific; does not indicate type of testing, tools used, or results

weak_bullet_ids.original: Made a small Python script to clean CSV files for a class assignment.
weak_bullet_ids.problem: Irrelevant to frontend role and lacks measurable impact

rewrites.original: Did a project on web development using HTML, CSS and some JavaScript.
rewrites.improved: Developed a static website using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to showcase responsive design concepts.
rewrites.why_better: Replaces vague verb "Did" with "Developed", specifies the artifact (static website) and purpose (responsive design), using only listed technologies.

rewrites.original: Worked on the company website and fixed bugs.
rewrites.improved: Diagnosed and resolved front‑end bugs on Brightline Softwares’ website, enhancing page stability.
rewrites.why_better: Uses stronger actions "Diagnosed and resolved", adds context (front‑end bugs, company name) and outcome (enhanced stability) without adding new data.

rewrites.improved: Assisted QA by executing functional tests on new website features, ensuring cross‑browser compatibility.
rewrites.why_better: Specifies the testing type (functional), the target (new website features), and the result (cross‑browser compatibility), improving clarity and relevance.

rewrites.original: Made a small Python script to clean CSV files for a class assignment.
rewrites.improved: Created a Python script to automate CSV cleaning for a class assignment, streamlining data preparation.
rewrites.why_better: Swaps weak verb "Made" for "Created", clarifies automation purpose and benefit (streamlining data preparation) while staying within listed skills.

auto_note: score 52; flagged TypeScript, REST, Jest, CI/CD; 3 rewrites, none invented a metric
